ConocoPhillips rose 0.96% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions. News broke on October 28th that the U.S. was reportedly preparing for potential strikes against Iran following the midterm elections, pushing crude prices higher — U.S. oil closed at $103.37 per barrel, up sharply from earlier in the week. The geopolitical risk premium from a possible prolonged conflict in the region drove investor demand for energy stocks as a hedge.

The move fits a broader two-week rally in the stock (up 4.94%), which tracks the energy sector's gains as oil prices have jumped on Iran-related conflict concerns. A notable gap remains between U.S. crude at $103 and global benchmarks at $123, suggesting international supply disruption fears are also pricing in potential Middle East supply losses.
